explanation.text:
Shiggaion--a plaintive song or elegy. Though obscure in details, this title seems to intimate that the occasion of this Psalm was some event in David's persecution by Saul. He prays for relief because he is innocent, and God will be glorified in his vindication. He thus passes to the celebration of God's righteous government, in defending the upright and punishing the wicked, whose malignant devices will result in their own ruin; and, confident of God's aid, he closes with rejoicing. (Psa. 7:1-17)

Though many enemies set upon him, one is singled out as prominent, and compared to a wild beast tearing his prey to pieces (compare Sa1 20:1; Sa1 23:23; Sa1 26:19).

bsb.title: A Shiggaion of David, which he sang to the LORD concerning the words of Cush, a Benjamite.
bsb.text: O LORD my God, I take refuge in You; save me and deliver me from all my pursuers,
or they will shred my soul like a lion and tear me to pieces with no one to rescue me.

explanation.text: if I have done this--that is, the crime charged in the "words of Cush" (compare Sa1 24:9).

bsb.text: O LORD my God, if I have done this, if injustice is on my hands,

explanation.text:
If I have injured my friend.

yea, I have delivered, etc.--This makes a good sense, but interrupts the course of thought, and hence it is proposed to render, "if I have spoiled my enemy"--in either case (compare Sa1 24:4-17; Sa1 31:8, Sa1 31:11).

bsb.text: if I have rewarded my ally with evil, if I have plundered my foe without cause,

explanation.text:
This is the consequence, if such has been his conduct.

mine honour--(compare Psa 3:3; Psa 4:2) --my personal and official dignity.

bsb.text: then may my enemy pursue me and overtake me; may he trample me to the ground and leave my honor in the dust. Selah

explanation.text:
God is involved as if hitherto careless of him (Psa 3:7; Psa 9:18).

rage--the most violent, like a flood rising over a river's banks.

the judgment . . . commanded--or, "ordained"; a just decision.

bsb.text: Arise, O LORD, in Your anger; rise up against the fury of my enemies. Awake, my God, and ordain judgment.

explanation.text:
compass thee--as those seeking justice.

return thou on high--assume the judgment seat, to be honored as a just Ruler by them.

bsb.text: Let the assembled peoples gather around You; take Your seat over them on high.

explanation.text: Though not claiming innocence in general, he can confidently do so in this case, and in demanding from the Judge of all the earth a judgment, he virtually asks acquittal.

bsb.text: The LORD judges the peoples; vindicate me, O LORD, according to my righteousness and integrity.

explanation.text: the hearts and reins--the affections and motives of men, or the seat of them (compare Psa 16:7; Psa 26:2); as we use heart and bosom or breast.

bsb.text: Put an end to the evil of the wicked, but establish the righteous, O righteous God who searches hearts and minds.
My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart.

explanation.text:
judgeth--as in Psa 7:8.

the wicked--Though not expressed, they are implied, for they alone are left as objects of anger.

bsb.text: God is a righteous judge and a God who feels indignation each day.

explanation.text: They are here distinctly pointed out, though by changing the person, a very common mode of speech, one is selected as a representative of wicked men generally. The military figures are of obvious meaning.

bsb.text: If one does not repent, God will sharpen His sword; He has bent and strung His bow.

explanation.text: against the persecutors--Some render "for burning," but the former is the best sense. Arrows for burning would be appropriate in besieging a town, not in warring against one man or a company in open fight.

bsb.text: He has prepared His deadly weapons; He ordains His arrows with fire.

explanation.text: The first clause expresses the general idea that wicked men labor to do evil, the others carry out the figure fully.

bsb.text: Behold, the wicked man travails with evil; he conceives trouble and births falsehood.

explanation.text: psa 7:15Sa1 18:17; Sa1 31:2 illustrate the statement whether alluded to or not. These verses are expository of Psa 7:14, showing how the devices of the wicked end in disappointment, falsifying their expectations.

bsb.text: He has dug a hole and hollowed it out; he has fallen into a pit of his own making.

explanation.text:
His mischief shall return upon his own head,.... That which he conceived and devised in his mind, and attempted to bring upon others, shall fall upon himself, as a just judgment from heaven upon him;

and his violent dealing shall come down upon his own pate; referring to the violence with which Saul pursued David, which would be requited to him, and of which he prophesied, 1 Samuel 26:10.

bsb.text: His trouble recoils on himself, and his violence falls on his own head.

explanation.text:
his righteousness-- (Psa 5:8). Thus illustrated in the defense of His servant and punishment of the wicked.

bsb.text: I will thank the LORD for His righteousness and sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High.
